title: Information Gathered About the Detective Boys
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, the other four Detective Boys, Takagi, Megure) omitted by convention, matching the old case file's own choice to exclude the Detective Boys despite being the interview's pretext. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. The old lower-fidelity case file got the culprit right (Atsushi Inaba) -- no correction needed there -- but it undercounted the cast: it omitted Kobayashi-sensei (Conan's homeroom teacher, who is herself one of the four alibi-message suspects and gets briefly accused on-screen) and Hayashi (Koeikan's editor-in-chief, whose voice on the reused year-old recording is the actual mechanism of the fake alibi and whose hay-fever/weather remarks are what crack it). It also collapsed all three cleared suspects' distinguishing alibi-breaking logic into flat `knows` edges; this rebuild keeps each suspect's specific clearance mechanism (missing railroad-crossing sound, conductor's hay-fever timing, year-old recording tell) as its own `clue` node. Temporal fields intentionally omitted per current build policy. case_type: murder.

attrs.cleared_reason: a real killer would have rushed to the body to plant misleading hair/prints, not left a normal callback message

attrs.symptom: hay fever, mistaken by himself for a cold

attrs.feature: four messages; blood smeared off the power button

attrs.origin: Inaba's genuine call to Koeikan a year earlier, also on April 22
attrs.giveaway: references rain and low pollen, contradicting this year's dry sunny April 22

attrs.damage: scratched by Higaki against a telephone pole

attrs.reason: bought to replace a blood-stained pair

attrs.finding: victim's blood found on the handlebars

clues.desc: Haruka's message has background TV audio but no railroad-crossing bell, though a train passes near the apartment daily around then -- proves she called from far away, not the apartment.
Higaki's on-board announcement cuts off mid-sentence (a sneezing hay-fever conductor who only started that shift after 11am) -- too late for him to have been near the apartment at 11:27.
Inaba's message names the date but never the year; its rain and low-pollen references match last year's April 22, not this dry sunny one -- proves the recording is a year old.
Blood is smeared off the answering machine's power button, but there is none on Sugimori's own fingers -- someone else pressed it after he died.

edges.motive_type: professional_betrayal (3-year corruption scoop sold to a rival magazine without consulting him)
